text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The road accident at Pala, which took the lives of eight children, may have been caused by the inexperience of the lorry driver, who was driving this type of vehicle for the first time, police investigators said. The government intends a nation-wide mourning on the day of burial, October 16.

- Estonia's aim for full membership of the EU and NATO means it wants to be reunited with Europe and integration with the democratic world, President Lennart Meri said at the session of the Trilateral Commission in Helsinki.

- Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian Defence ministers signed in Riga a joint declaration on the further development of the Baltic battallion but not a declaration on forming a joint naval force BALTRON for participating in international peacekeeping operations.

- Estonian-Latvian relations have reached a new stage, Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said on his return from a visit to Estonia. Estonian President Lennart Meri's two-day state visit to Latvia will begin on October 23.
- A ten day pre-electoral voting for members of the local councils began October 10.

- A concert-charity event with 235 1,000-kroon tickets in the Estonia hall was intended to raise funds for Estonian Cancer Association; a donation of 270,000 kroons was delivered from the Swedish Cancer Association.
- Fuel companies Neste and Statoil raised petrol prices by 15 Estonian cents, saying that world oil prices have risen.
